speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The House is gathered here to acknowledge the achievements of Team Singapore at the Rio 2016 Paralympic Games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our Paralympians, with their incredible feats in Rio, have uplifted the nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Beyond medals, each Paralympian has shown us what it means to be a champion – to be counted among the world's best and fly our flag high at the world's biggest stage for para sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These 13 extraordinary athletes have shown us that with hard work and sacrifice, we can realise our dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Their achievements also exemplify how a nation as small as ours can punch above its weight.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I am honoured to have witnessed some of their amazing and inspiring performances in Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They were in impressive form at the Games and beat the teams from Greece and Portugal, the gold and silver medallists respectively, from the 2012 Paralympic Games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While Nurul and Sze Ning were disappointed they could not bring back a Paralympic medal this time, I believe that they will grow stronger from this experience and do better in future.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Nur Syahidah Alim was a double gold medallist at the ASEAN Para Games and became our first archer ever to compete at the Paralympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In the lead-up to the Paralympics, Syahidah trained six hours per day, six times a week.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Her result in the Women's Individual Compound event was testament to her hard work and determination.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Her round of 16 match pitted her against an athlete ranked fourth in the Ranking Round.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Despite some problems with her stool which affected her stability, she held her nerves and went on to beat her opponent.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: She also put up a tremendous fight in the quarter-final match.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Facing the eventual bronze medallist in unpredictable wind conditions, she lost the match by just two points, that is, 135 versus 137.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: She displayed great sportsmanship, always having a smile on her face and was a crowd favourite.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Equestrian team of Laurentia Tan, Maximillian Tan and Gemma Rose Foo had to contend with serious injury setbacks in the months leading up to the Paralympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Laurentia injured her spine, Maximillian hurt his hip joint, while Gemma ruptured a spleen.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: But that did not deter our riders, who continued to train hard, sometimes in pain, to represent Singapore in Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Their courage, determination and fighting spirit certainly filled us all with pride.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They showed us the importance of perseverance in the things we are passionate about, and that a positive attitude is often the best medicine for unexpected setbacks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: At 39 years young and a Paralympic Games debutant, Norsilawati Sa'at is an inspiration to us all.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: She has shown us that age is certainly not a barrier to sports and excellence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Despite taking a break from wheelchair racing in 2011 and returning only last year, Sila made tremendous progress to qualify for the Paralympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Besides her pet event, the 100-metre T52, she was also extended an invitation to participate in the Women's 400-metre T52 Finals so that the race could proceed with the minimum of five competitors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: She graciously accepted the invitation, gave it her all, and finished with a personal best time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our long-jumper, Suhairi Suhani, is the baby of the team at just 19 years old.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Known by those around him to be a model athlete, Suhairi never complained and only wanted to learn and keep improving.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With his discipline and positive attitude, he achieved a personal best in the Men's Long Jump T20 Final in his Paralympics debut.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: After winning a gold medal at the China Open Athletics Championships earlier this year, Diroy Noordin made his Paralympics debut in the Men's Javelin and Shot Put events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I am certain that Diroy will continue to inspire other persons with disabilities to believe in themselves and pursue their dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We look forward to stronger performances from Suhairi and Diroy at future events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our Sailors, Jovin Tan and Yap Qian Yin, had to contend with not just the world-class competitors, but harsh weather and rough seas.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: After a commendable showing in the earlier races, our sailors, unfortunately, had to be withdrawn for safety reasons towards the end of the competition although they steadfastly wanted to soldier on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Last, but not least, we have our Swimmers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Theresa Goh is one of our most experienced Paralympians.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: After more than a decade of sweat and tears, months spent training and competing overseas, and hour after hour spent in the pool, she finally won her first Paralympic medal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It was a long and hard journey, but I think she would agree that it was all worth it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To us all, Theresa is a symbol of commitment, resolve and dedication.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: She even broke the world record in the Women's 100-metre S2 Final.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These were unforgettable moments as the Singapore flag was hoisted and Majulah Singapura was played in the Olympic Aquatics Stadium in Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Despite her achievements, she is always humble, grounded and appreciative of the support from her friends and family.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To all our aspiring athletes, Theresa and Pin Xiu are perfect role models.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To Singaporeans, they represent the sporting heroes that we all look up to.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: My warmest congratulations to all the athletes again!

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I would also like to acknowledge Mr Ho Cheng Kwee, Chef-de-Mission of our Paralympic contingent, for his leadership and commitment in ensuring the athletes' well-being at the Games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It was heartening to also see the outpouring of pride and appreciation from Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We saw a large crowd at Changi Airport cheering and welcoming our Paralympians as they touched down from Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We saw even more lining the streets during the celebratory parade.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Among them was nine-year-old Teo Choon Khang, who has been taking swimming lessons since he was three, even though he has cerebral palsy.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Pin Xiu said after her win that, "Nothing is impossible as long as you set your mind to it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It might not be the goal that you will eventually hope to get but, along the way, through the process, you will learn many things about yourself   other things that will  .

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It's better than not having tried at all." Indeed, we are proud of our Paralympians' achievements, but we are even prouder of the fact that they have taken the plunge, sacrificed so much, and done so with such courage and tenacity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They are not constrained by their limitations but are instead driven towards what is possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In my many years watching and supporting sports, I have never seen such levels of interest and support for our para-athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Not only will this be the new norm, I believe that the support will grow from strength to strength.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: What more can I say about Pin Xiu, Theresa, Syahidah, Norsilawati, Suhairi, Diroy, Nurul, Sze Ning, Laurentia, Max, Gemma, Jovin and Qian Yin that has not been said.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Many of us were not able to be there in Rio to support you, but I hope you heard us cheering you on thousands of miles away, where many of us watched you intently on the screens and followed your exploits via social media.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: You united us as one people regardless of where we were in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I remember each one of your beaming faces as you arrived back home in Singapore at Changi Airport, starting with Suhairi who surely has the most infectious smile ever.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Your Rio journey was clearly uplifting but, perhaps even more significantly, you created something special for all of us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: How many of us have the privilege and honour to wear our national colours and to fly our flag at competitions?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: How many of us can display the sheer grit and determination that can inspire so many?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: How many of us can galvanise a community and pull people together?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: You are, first and foremost, our Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: You enabled us to see the true you – the person behind the physical being.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: You have been our role models, demonstrating resilience and an indomitable spirit, showing us what is possible through dedication and hard work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For many of you, it is not just about your quest for personal achievement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is about our community of persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Pin Xiu shared that she would not have continued this journey if she was doing it for herself.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: She wants to share this message with all Singaporeans: that you can get there if you want it bad enough.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The same goes for all our para-athletes who want to show that anything is possible if you try and work towards it and, most importantly, to believe in yourself.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There is another group of champions whom I want to recognise – the family and friends of our Paralympians.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: You have shown great support and are clearly the number one fans of our para-athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Your love and sacrifice have enabled them to realise their dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: You are always there to cheer them on and are their pillars of support through ups and downs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Theresa's parents, Mr Bernard Goh and Mdm Rose Mok, firmly believe in the value of sports, and that every child, able-bodied or disabled, has his or her unique strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They believe that sports brought more opportunities for their children to make friends and to form a support group which helped them develop and become stronger socially, emotionally and mentally.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Sze Ning's mother, Mdm Tan Ngoek Moi, shared in two interviews – I gathered her various comments and put them together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And she shared this about Sze Ning when she was young: "Everyone said to me, ‘Why don't you just abandon her?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Don't be so hard on yourself." But she said later, "I'm happy and proud to see her all grown up.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: She already did her best and came in fourth overall.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have to use our sincerity to motivate them because they are our children and we understand them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And we, as parents, we have to help them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: If we don't, no one else will." For our para-athletes and their families, it is not just in the competitions that they have to strive hard.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is also in the race of life that they cross seemingly insurmountable hurdles, dealing with the simplest of tasks that so many of us just take for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: All of you, not just our athletes, but all our Singaporeans with disabilities and special needs, you have changed us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While we have made some progress towards a more inclusive society, we are definitely not there yet.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We want to be a people who see the person first before the disability.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We want to be able to care, to be compassionate and to love.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In big and small ways, never under-estimate the difference that we can make, whether as family members, classmates, employers, neighbours or simply as members of the public.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: All it takes is consideration in the buildings that we build, in the workplaces that we establish, in the community that we live in and in our everyday lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And most importantly, it is in our hearts and minds that we need to just embrace our fellow Singaporeans of any ability for who they are.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Because by being who you are and championing the way forward, you help us all become better selves and perhaps, in turn, to begin to build a better Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They must have also persevered through muscle fatigue, injuries as they built up physical and mental stamina among the team.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: All these in preparation for the ultimate sporting experience that the Paralympic Games gives.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It was already a victory that our Paralympians got to their start lines.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because each Paralympian converted adversity into a will to excel and, in so doing, made Singaporeans very proud.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Your sturdy will in Archery, Athletics, Boccia, Equestrian, Sailing, Swimming is what we are celebrating today.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What you did out there at the Paralympic Games also spoke of the value of participation and training hard to better one's own personal best.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Yes, you had excelled to get to the start line.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Yes, you were already joyful in achieving that.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Yet, not quite satisfied, you pushed yourself further and further to improve.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That extra push was, in and of itself, remarkable, perhaps arising from a divine discontent.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Yet, you the Paralympians displayed the personal integrity imbedded in the very meaning of sportsmanship: to strive to outdo one's own limits for a cause greater than oneself.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I learnt that meaning of sportsmanship from Chaoyang School students about 20 years ago.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The school, which provides education for children with special needs, required assistance with its sports programmes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I was playing Hockey at the time and the school asked if I could help coach its Hockey team made up of young students between eight and 12 years old.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That team was preparing for its own tournament amongst special needs students.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Some of the children found it difficult to run.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For some, it was not easy to hold a stick, yet they played their hearts out, learnt from one another, improved their skills and celebrated whenever a teammate scored because it meant Chaoyang School was doing well.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That group of young Singaporean students reflected the very spirit our Paralympians displayed on the world stage at Rio 2016: the value of participation, the value of outdoing one's own limits and the value of doing so for a cause greater than oneself.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There is much we can learn from that, especially in education, especially in our schools where achievements should be celebrated when the child has done that child's best.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Before Rio 2016, Pin Xiu shared, "I decided that I should really excel as much as possible when my body still allows me, by pushing myself to the limits for Singapore".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: You were already victorious at your start line.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: After Rio 2016, you shared your reflections with Singaporeans, "We athletes have doubts sometimes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We don't know if today is a good day for our bodies.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It was really just a lot of mental strength to go at my fastest ever, and to compete against myself and my previous times".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Rejoicing in accomplishments already achieved, yet not quite satisfied, and so, wanting to push for a cause beyond oneself.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: She said, "I had a lot of moments where I thought of giving up.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But it took a lot of mental skills and encouragement from people telling me that I could do it and to be positive.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I had to convince myself, talk to myself and remind myself that I had done a lot of hard work.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is not just my work, I have a big team behind me and if I had a list of people to thank, I would not be able to finish it.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I conclude, Madam, with firm support for the Motion standing in the name of Minister Grace Fu.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But we are not only celebrating those achievements.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: All of us who have watched or read about you in action, are moved and inspired by your never-say-die attitude to overcoming difficulties in life to follow your dreams through sheer grit and perseverance.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For Theresa Goh, this has been a 17-year journey and continuing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Paralympian effort is single-minded in a way that few of us will ever understand – the sacrifices and struggles, the zero-compromise commitment you all have put in to prepare for the Games.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: These are lessons for us all – that we should not give up on our goals come what may, and that hard work and resilience pay.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Pin Xiu is a resident of mine and I have known her and her parents for a number of years.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Her parents are active participants in one of my community groups.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As we have seen in the case of Joseph Schooling and many other sportsmen and sportswomen, parents and family are the key to motivating our athletes, and we should do what we can to also acknowledge, recognise and support these parents.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: She shared the story of her mother in a video, and she said this of her mother: "You have given me the strength to be who I am.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: You have taught me what it's like to love a family.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: You have brought joy and pride to all Singaporeans and also taught us many important lessons.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Paralympic Games is the highest-level global competition for our athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also wish to honour other athletes who trained hard but, for some reason, did not make it to Rio.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: When Theresa Goh won her bronze in Rio, her good friend and fellow medallist, Yip Pin Xiu, embraced and told her that nobody will know what they have gone through these 17 years.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Indeed, many of us can only read about it but never really know the terrain of the arduous road to Rio – the gruelling trainings and the sacrifices behind a sporting career on the world stage.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These stories are not uncommon amongst the rest of the athletes: Nurul, Sze Ning, Suhairi, Muhammad Diroy, Maximillian, Laurentia, Gemma, Jovin, Qian Yin, Pin Xiu and Theresa.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Hence, to the Paralympians, thank you for showing us the power of the human spirit.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Like the proverbial bumblebee which aerodynamically is not supposed to be able to fly, but it flies anyway.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: You are our very own Singaporean athletes with disabilities – disabilities which, instead of tripping you, have helped the rest of Singapore, open their eyes and see your true and powerful abilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: You face greater challenges than typical athletes and deserve recognition similar to or even beyond them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: From you, we learnt the lessons of mental toughness, true grit, optimism and self-control.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I pray that you will guard sacredly this privileged leadership position or space that you occupy.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know that many of you do not want to be defined by your disability and want to be seen, first, as athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But it is the unique identity, the package that you come in, abilities and disabilities combined, that enrich, humble and inspire the rest of us Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: If you can do it, then perhaps the rest of us can rise above our daily ailments, grievances and complaints and take on life the way you do, against the odds; making lemonades of the lemons we are handed in life.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, Paralympians, I urge you to be the evangelists for a better world – encourage others to do sports on a daily level; tell them how not to let what you cannot do prevent you from what you can; and how not to let failures deter you for longer than they should.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, to the usually unsung heroes behind our athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I believe in the life-view that, in life, that everything we achieve in life, somebody helped us.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is thus also my privilege to congratulate and thank the people who have been supporting the Paralympians.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: First, the family members who had raised these young people and cheered them on in life, medals or not.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I believe that no child with special needs, comes to a family by accident – no child anyway.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It takes a special kind of human spirit to embrace a child with special needs in the family, give him space to pursue his passion whilst worrying about his future.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Families of our special athletes, too, deserve a medal, in my book.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, lest we forget, the supporting teams from the SNPC – the then Chairman Dr Teo-Koh Sock Miang; Mr Ho Cheng Kwee, who is not able to come today, Chef-de-Mission of the 2016 Rio Paralympic Games, the SDSC, the Singapore National Olympic Council, Sports Singapore and the Singapore Sports Institute.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many are the unsung heroes who worked tirelessly behind the scenes to make the road to Rio possible.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: To the rest of Singapore, I ask you to continue to look beyond the disabilities and celebrate the abilities of our Paralympians and other athletes and the rest of the special needs community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But beyond the carnival and celebrations, what the organisers deeply yearn for is a transformed society that truly embraces persons with special needs in every aspect of Singapore life.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Is there enough support, beyond awareness, to cause a change in our behaviours towards those who are different?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Do we know persons with special needs only when they become celebrated Paralympians?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Do we, in our social network, have any true friends with special needs?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Do we, at our workplace, treat those with special needs with dignity and not pity?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In many ways, people with special needs are like you and I, with similar needs and aspirations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of them simply want to have access to opportunities in life, like the rest of us.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, let us go beyond compassion and adjust our lenses and behaviours to create schools, workplaces, public places of interest where persons with special needs are not just talked about, but seen, heard and their presence felt daily.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On that note, I want to salute again the Paralympians and all those who stood and are still standing behind you.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: You are some of our most important torchbearers for a better world.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Much earlier, after Pin Xiu won the 2008 Paralympic Gold medal, you moved us when you said, "This is my favourite medal, because it is Singapore's first Paralympic gold medal and, with it, I did Singapore proud".

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: You did Singapore proud, all of you did and we are all very, very proud of you.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I also thank and congratulate the greater Team Singapore of caregivers, loved ones, officials, trainers, coaches, friends, teammates, sponsors and supporters.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: We have come far since we first participated in the 1988 Summer Paralympics.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: But we continued to send our athletes to the Summer Paralympics.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Over the years, we have come to recognise the value of sports in achieving our national priorities in developing healthy and resilient people, forging strong united communities, retaining core values, sharing memories, strengthening friendships and building a dynamic society and a dynamic economy.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: We did not do enough for our athletes and para-athletes in our earlier years.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: It is my hope that with Vision 2030, with the Disability Sports Master Plan and the new National Outdoor Adventure Education Masterplan, sports will become more inclusive.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: And as we continue to conceptualise and implement, it must always be a work in progress.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: We should be open to learn from other countries, such as the United Kingdom and Canada, known to provide good support for their athletes with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: It has taken us a long time to associate sports and disability, or should I say, sports and medical conditions.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Frankie returned with a bronze medal and Robert did us proud in his placings.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: In 1975, the duo represented Singapore again and, this time, they won gold and bronze medals.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: We did not just start winning sports medals on the international scene.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Through the years, our para-athletes have been doing us proud.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: It is just that we did not know that much about them.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: And we are, slowly, gaining national consciousness on this issue, thanks to everyone who persevered – all of our para-athletes and their loved ones, and their officials.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: And to the younger ones in this Chamber today, our Paralympians – as you enjoy the recognition and the challenges that are ahead of you, remember all those who went before you, who gave of their best despite having a lot less.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Remember that they paved the way for you as well.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: And as you remember those who went before you, we will also remember the lessons that we have learnt from you.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: You put us in the international limelight in the world of Paralympics – tiny Singapore.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Your achievements made us sit up and realise that persons with disabilities, even from tiny Singapore, can make their mark in the sports world.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: By your medal wins, you gave Singaporeans a chance to be inspired; inspired by your grit to endure physical pain, by your intelligence, your determination to push the limits, to succeed.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: But even then, for all the interviews that you gave, for all the inspirational talks that you gave, we can never imagine all the pain, tears, frustrations and sacrifices that you had to make.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: We can never imagine the pain of the injuries, what sacrifices you made in your education, your career, your social activities, what sacrifices your parents made for you, what financial burdens you had to bear and what opportunities you lost.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: You have inspired us and you have made me very, very proud of you, not just because you won medals, but because all of you trained and sacrificed, and even if you never got to the Games, even if competed but you did not win, you never give up.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I am proud of you because you are not afraid of your weak bodies.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I am inspired by you because you have strong minds and stout hearts.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: And I am humbled by the lessons that I learn from you.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Theresa says of her disabilities, "I'm fine with it.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I wouldn't be swimming or where I am today if I weren't disabled." I believe you spoke not just for yourself, but for all your colleagues.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Paralympians, you turned your disability into opportunity, and made your disability your success.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that as we salute you for your medals, many more would, like us, salute you for rising above all your failures.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Muhammad Diroy – he also happens to be SPD's Youth Aspiration Award 2015 winner.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: He was initially not selected to represent Singapore at the Paralympics.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: He continued and he stuck to his regime of training three times a week to keep improving, to do his best for other upcoming competitions.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: He became a last-minute addition to the Singapore contingent.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Jovin Tan, our para-sailor, said this, "Life is always about trying and not giving up.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Even if you are the last boat, you should try to think of possible ways to climb one or two more positions up".

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Laurentia says, "Our glorious moments are not in never failing, but in rising every time we fall".

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: It is about not allowing setbacks to set us back.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: And it is about doing our best no matter what.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Unfortunately, that is not glamorous but that will outlast the shine on your medals.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: When Paralympians won medals, the public debated greater rewards for medallists, greater support for para-athletes.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: You rose above monetary rewards and you said you did not do it for the money.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, I firmly believe that our athletes did not do it for the money.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: More than cash payment, it is also about inclusion.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: The best of Government schemes will not be good enough if we do not play our part to support our para-athletes.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Yes, a great part of that has got to do with funds, more sponsorship, but how do we get sponsors if there are no spectators?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Here is one opportunity for us to just be a spectator.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: We give them hope, we let them know that there are people behind them when times are tough.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: By that, we also tell the corporate entities that there is value in sponsoring our athletes.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Get to the stadium, the swimming pools, wherever the events are held.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Can we be, if nothing else, a spectator?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: It has been a long journey and it will continue to be.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: As Pin Xiu said to Theresa when the latter won her bronze medal at the Paralympics, "Nobody knows our journey like us, and I am so incredibly proud of you." And now, I say this, and I am sure my colleagues here in this House will join me in saying this: indeed, nobody knows your journey like you, but you know what?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: And with that, Madam, I support the Motion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Truth be told, most of us do not know much about the Paralympic Games.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We muddle over how para-athletes are classified by disability and find it puzzling that there are so many similar events.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, it is impossible for able-bodied persons to get into the mind of a disabled person, let alone one who dares to put himself or herself out there in the arena in front of the whole world.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As Ms Theresa Goh once said, "I wouldn't be swimming or where I am today if I weren't disabled." Madam, there are many inspiring stories all over the world about how individuals overcame disability through sports.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: A few days ago, I heard over the radio about a Canadian teenager named Trent Seymour, a very promising softball pitcher and catcher, who was paralysed in a hunting accident two years ago at age 16.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: After weeks in the intensive care unit and months of rehabilitation, he decided that he wanted to return to the game he loved, even though he was now a paraplegic.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: He signed up for umpire training and passed the required tests and soon, he was the first ever Umpire on Wheels.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The sight of him on softball pitches surprised and inspired many fans worldwide.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Their children were glued to their television sets every day and night, rooting for our Paralympic athletes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Some of these parents had introduced sports to their children as therapy.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Now, their children were seeing before their very own eyes that, through sporting competition, they, too, could, one day, don the national colours and bring glory to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It goes without saying that cultivating our para-athletes to sporting excellence takes a whole village and the Government as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I would like to move the Motion.
